title: Karos-Eperjesszög cemeteries
fact_summary: A group of 10th-century conqueror-period cemeteries in north-east Hungary, the source of many of the genetic samples from that period.

place.label: North-east Hungary
place.note: Pin placed by Claude in north-east Hungary, the region the study names. The cemeteries' exact position has not been checked.

claims.text: A 2020 study calls Karos-Eperjesszög in north-east Hungary “a special site complex”, and says 76% of the conquest-period samples it discusses came from there.
claims.certainty_reason: Read in the study's introduction. Which set of samples the 76% refers to is Claude's reading of the context.

claims.text: A 2019 study took 24 of its 29 conquest-period samples from four nearby cemeteries: Karos 1, 2 and 3, and Kenézlő.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Three conquerors buried at Karos II share a maternal lineage link with the individual Uyelgi3 from the Trans-Ural region.

sources.locator: The possible maternal genetic connection of South-Ural region's populations and the Hungarian conquerors

claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

dating_methods.text: The 2020 study treats the Karos II individuals as tenth-century Hungarian conquerors.
